card.name: Risk wording in boxed warnings
card.fires_on: Responds to the word right after a risk phrase in warning text: 'than' after 'more susceptible to infections', and 'stroke' after 'myocardial infarction and'.

modes.label: Comparison after infection risk
modes.description: The word 'than' ending a phrase about being more susceptible to infections than healthy people.
modes.example: that suppress the immune system are more susceptible to infections<< than>> healthy individuals.

modes.label: Stroke in NSAID warning
modes.description: The word 'stroke' closing the list of cardiovascular events in the NSAID boxed warning.
modes.example: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) cause an increased risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, including myocardial infarction and<< stroke>>, which can be fatal. This risk

card.writes: It lowers the odds of emergency and rescue-care words, with no clear boost to any one word.
card.plain: It marks the end of a stated risk in a warning, such as stroke or infection risk, where emergency-care words are less likely to come next.
